question:
Refer to the exhibit. An engineer is implementing an ERSPAN configuration to mirror web server traffic connected to N7K-2. Which ERSPAN configuration must be applied on N7K-1 to forward traffic to the network analyzer?
! ERSPAN Source Configuration
N7k-2(config)# monitor session 1 type erspan-source
N7k-2(config-erspan-src)# erspan-id 100
N7k-2(config-erspan-src)# vrf default
N7k-2(config-erspan-src)# destination ip 192.168.16.55
N7k-2(config-erspan-src)# source interface ethernet 2/10
N7k-2(config-erspan-src)# no shut
N7k-2(config-erspan-src)# exit
N7k-2(config)# monitor erspan origin ip-address 192.168.16.10 global
context: Topology: N7K-1 (192.168.16.55) has Eth1/5 to Network Analyzer (10.10.11.1) and Eth1/30.10 to IP Cloud (L3), which connects to N7K-2 (Eth2/10 to Web Server).
imageNote: Diagram: N7K-1 (192.168.16.55) has Eth1/5 to Network Analyzer (10.10.11.1) and Eth1/30.10 to an IP Cloud (L3), which connects to N7K-2 (Eth2/10 to Web Server).
options:
monitor session 1 type erspan-destination
source interface ethernet 1/30.10
destination interface ethernet 1/30
erspan-id 100
vrf default
no shut

monitor session 1 type erspan-destination
source vlan 10
destination interface ethernet 1/5
erspan-id 100
vrf default
no shut

monitor session 1 type erspan-destination
source interface ethernet 1/30
destination ip 10.10.11.1
erspan-id 100
vrf default
no shut

monitor session 1 type erspan-destination
source ip 192.168.16.55
destination interface ethernet 1/5
erspan-id 100
vrf default
no shut
theory: An ERSPAN destination session terminates the GRE-encapsulated mirrored traffic and replays the original frames out a local interface toward the analyzer; it must be told which ERSPAN source IP to expect the tunnel from, using source ip to match the origin address the source switch used, and which local interface to forward the decapsulated copy out, using destination interface, matching the erspan-id that ties the destination session to the specific source session on the remote switch. Using a VLAN or a routed interface as the source of a destination session, or sending decapsulated traffic back out to a remote IP, doesn't match how an ERSPAN destination session is actually built. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — ERSPAN Destination Session Configuration)
